mainTopic: Items that forbid a mixture in any amount, and the law of יין נסך that falls into a cistern of wine.
overview: The first משנה lists items that are forbidden and that forbid any mixture they fall into, even in a tiny amount. The גמרא asks what these items share. It concludes that each one is both a דבר שבמנין (an item counted one by one) and an איסור הנאה (forbidden for any benefit). Other items that seem to fit, such as אגוזי פרך, רימוני בדן and a homeowner's loaves, are left out because they are already taught in מסכת ערלה. A second משנה rules that יין נסך falling into a cistern forbids the whole cistern for benefit. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees: the whole cistern may be sold to a גוי, minus the value of the forbidden wine. רב follows him only when a barrel is lost among barrels. שמואל and several other אמוראים follow him even when wine mixed into wine. רב נחמן gives the practical הלכה: real יין נסך mixed as liquid is forbidden, a barrel among barrels may be sold, and סתם יינם may be sold even when mixed as liquid.

steps.title: The list of items that forbid a mixture in any amount
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists eleven items that are forbidden and that make a mixture forbidden no matter how small their share.
steps.simpleTranslation: These items are forbidden, and even the smallest amount of them makes a mixture forbidden: wine poured for idol worship, objects of idol worship, hides torn at the heart for idol worship, an ox sentenced to stoning, the heifer whose neck is broken, the birds of a מצורע, the hair of a נזיר, a firstborn donkey, meat cooked in milk, the goat sent away on יום כיפור, and ordinary animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a list of forbidden things that are so strict that they forbid a whole mixture, even if they make up only a tiny part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a forbidden item that gets mixed into a large majority of permitted items can become בטל (cancelled out). The items on this list never become בטל: one of them mixed into a thousand permitted ones still forbids them all. The משנה does not say why these items are special, and that is exactly what the גמרא will ask next.

keyTerms.meaning: They make a mixture forbidden in any amount, even a tiny one
Wine poured as an offering to an idol
Animal hides with a tear opposite the heart, from an idol-worship practice
An ox sentenced to be stoned for killing a person
The heifer whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
Non-sacred animals slaughtered inside the Temple courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbidden in any amount' here does not mean you may not eat even a crumb of it (that is a different topic). It means that the item can never be cancelled out (בטל) in a mixture, so it forbids everything it is mixed with.

phrases.english: MISHNA: These are forbidden,
and they make a mixture forbidden in any amount:
libation wine, and idol worship,
and hides torn at the heart,
phrases.notes: These are hides with a hole opposite the heart, a sign that the heart was taken out for idol worship.

phrases.english: and an ox to be stoned, and a heifer whose neck is broken,
and the birds of a leper, and the hair of a nazirite,
and a firstborn donkey, and meat cooked in milk,
and the goat that is sent away,
phrases.notes: The goat sent off to the wilderness on יום כיפור (ויקרא 16).

phrases.english: and non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרִין וְאוֹסְרִין בְּכׇל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.english: these are forbidden and make a mixture forbidden in any amount.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eleven listed items are forbidden and are never cancelled out in a mixture; any amount of them forbids the whole mixture.

steps.title: If the rule is counted items, why leave out pieces of a carcass?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the common rule of the list is, and tests the first option: items that are counted (דבר שבמנין).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the תנא counting? If he is listing items that are counted, he should also have listed pieces of נבילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what rule ties the list together and suggests a first answer: maybe these are all items that are counted. It then attacks that idea right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דבר שבמנין is an item important enough to be counted one by one, and such an item does not become בטל in a mixture. But important pieces of נבילה are also counted items, and they are missing from the list. So 'counted items' alone cannot be the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he counting? What rule is behind the list?
An item that is counted one by one, so it is too important to be cancelled out
Let him also teach (it should have been on the list too)
Pieces of meat from an animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the tanna listing?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what is the one feature all these items share?

phrases.english: If he is listing items that are counted,
let him also teach pieces of a carcass!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא מַאי קָחָשֵׁיב? אִי דָּבָר שֶׁבְּמִנְיָן קָחָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the rule behind the משנה's list and tests the first possible rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the list's rule is 'items that are counted' (דבר שבמנין).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pieces of נבילה are also counted items, yet they are not on the list, so this cannot be the full rule.

steps.title: If the rule is benefit-forbidden items, why leave out חמץ on פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the second option: items you may not benefit from (איסורי הנאה), and finds a missing item.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is listing items that you may not benefit from, he should also have listed חמץ on פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second possible rule for the list and shows that it also does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item on the list is forbidden even for benefit, not only for eating. But חמץ בפסח is also forbidden for benefit, and it is not on the list. So 'benefit-forbidden items' alone cannot be the rule either, and the גמרא is now stuck between two options that both fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Items that you may not get any benefit or use from
Leavened food during פסח

phrases.english: If he is listing items forbidden for benefit,
let him also teach leavened bread on Passover!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same question: after the first rule fails, the second possible rule is tested and also fails.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the list's rule is 'items forbidden for benefit' (איסורי הנאה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חמץ בפסח is also forbidden for benefit, yet it is not on the list, so this cannot be the full rule.

steps.title: The list needs both features together
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא (or רבי יצחק נפחא) answers that the תנא only lists items that are both counted and forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said, and some say it was רבי יצחק נפחא: This תנא requires two things: the item must be counted, and it must be forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the list is not built on one feature but on two features together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pieces of נבילה are counted items but are not forbidden for benefit, so they are left out. חמץ בפסח is forbidden for benefit but is not a counted item, so it is also left out. Only items that have both features made it onto the list, which answers both questions at once.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds two things (he requires two conditions)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list = items that are both a דבר שבמנין AND an איסור הנאה. Having just one of the two features (like נבילה or חמץ בפסח) is not enough to get on this list.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for reading the whole משנה: each item on the list must have both features, and the following discussion is built on this answer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa:
This tanna holds two things —
an item that is counted and forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both questions from steps 2 and 3 with one combined rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining both suggested rules into one rule that needs both conditions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the list was built on just one feature, either counted items or benefit-forbidden items.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list needs both features at once, so נבילה (only counted) and חמץ בפסח (only benefit-forbidden) are correctly left out.

steps.title: Why aren't פרך nuts and בדן pomegranates on the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the list. אגוזי פרך and רימוני בדן fit both features, so why did the תנא leave them out?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא should also list פרך nuts and בדן pomegranates, since they are both counted items and forbidden for benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new rule from step 4 by pointing to items that fit it but are missing from the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the list holds everything that is both a דבר שבמנין and an איסור הנאה. אגוזי פרך and רימוני בדן are special fruits that are sold by count, and when they are ערלה it is forbidden to benefit from them. So they seem to belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him teach (why didn't the תנא include it?)
A special kind of nut with a brittle shell
Pomegranates from the place called בדן

phrases.english: But let him teach perekh nuts
and Badan pomegranates,
since they are a counted item and forbidden for benefit!
phrases.notes: They are forbidden for benefit when they grew in the tree's first three years (ערלה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 4 against items missing from the list
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list under the rule from step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These items meet both conditions, so the list looks incomplete.

steps.title: They were already taught in מסכת ערלה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא did not need to repeat them, because a משנה in ערלה already teaches that these items forbid a mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: He already taught it there: what can become ערלה makes the mixture ערלה, and what can become כלאי הכרם makes it כלאי הכרם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these fruits were left out on purpose, because their law appears in another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list here is not meant to cover every possible case. The משנה in ערלה already says these fruits are not cancelled out in a mixture, so there was no need to say it again here.

keyTerms.meaning: He already taught it there (in another place)
Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden for benefit
Forbidden mixed planting in a vineyard

phrases.english: He already taught it there:
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה in מסכת ערלה, chapter 3.

phrases.english: what is fit for orlah makes it orlah,
what is fit for kilei hakerem makes it kilei hakerem.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list should include every item that meets both conditions
steps.terutzMaskana: Items already taught in מסכת ערלה did not need to be repeated

steps.title: Why aren't a homeowner's loaves of חמץ on the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another missing item: a homeowner's loaves that are חמץ on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא should also list a homeowner's loaves, regarding חמץ on פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second item that seems to fit the rule but is missing from the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A homeowner's loaves are each special, so they can count as a counted item. חמץ on פסח is forbidden for benefit. So these loaves seem to meet both conditions.

keyTerms.meaning: A homeowner's loaves (each one is special, not mass-produced)
Leavened bread on פסח, which is forbidden for benefit

phrases.english: But let him teach a homeowner's loaves
regarding leavened bread on Pesach!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיתְנֵי כִּכָּרוֹת שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לְעִנְיַן חָמֵץ בְּפֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same kind as step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Homeowner's loaves of חמץ are both counted and forbidden for benefit, yet they are not listed.

steps.title: That is רבי עקיבא's view, taught elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי עקיבא holds that a homeowner's loaves are not cancelled out, and his view already appears in the משנה in ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who did you hear say this? רבי עקיבא. And that was already taught there: רבי עקיבא adds a homeowner's loaves as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this item is only רבי עקיבא's opinion, and it is already recorded in another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a homeowner's loaves are a counted item is not accepted by everyone. It belongs to רבי עקיבא. Since his addition is already written in מסכת ערלה, our משנה did not need to list it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who did you hear say this? (whose opinion is it?)
Adds (to the list)

phrases.english: Whom did you hear who says this?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ הָתָם:
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva, and he already taught it there:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מוֹסִיף אַף כִּכָּרוֹת שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva adds also a homeowner's loaves.

steps.terutzResolutionType: It is only one תנא's view, and it is already taught elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Homeowner's loaves should be on the list
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only רבי עקיבא's view, already stated in מסכת ערלה

steps.title: What do the closing words 'הרי אלו' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with the words 'these are...'. The גמרא asks what those words come to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'These' — what do they come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the closing words of the משנה and asks what they add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה says 'these' after a list, it suggests that only these items count and others do not. The גמרא wants to know which other items are being left out.

keyTerms.meaning: These are (the משנה's closing words)
To exclude what?

phrases.english: "These are" — to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list itself to its closing words
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'הרי אלו' leave out

steps.title: Items with only one of the two features are left out
steps.stepSummary: 'הרי אלו' leaves out an item that is counted but not forbidden for benefit, and an item that is forbidden for benefit but not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes a counted item that is not forbidden for benefit, and also an item that is forbidden for benefit but is not a counted item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'these' teaches that only items with both features forbid any mixture they fall into.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms the rule from step 4. The words 'הרי אלו' limit this משנה's rule to items that are both a דבר שבמנין and an איסור הנאה. An item with just one of the two features is not included in this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And not
Or also

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list holds only items that are both a דבר שבמנין and an איסור הנאה. Missing items were left out because they are taught in מסכת ערלה. 'הרי אלו' excludes anything with only one of the two features.

phrases.english: To exclude a counted item
that is not forbidden for benefit,
or also to exclude something forbidden for benefit
that is not a counted item.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי דָּבָר שֶׁבְּמִנְיָן וְלָאו אִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It excludes items that have only one of the two features
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both conditions are needed for an item to forbid a mixture no matter how small its share.

steps.title: Libation wine falls into a cistern: all of it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if יין נסך falls into a cistern of wine, the whole cistern is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If libation wine fell into a cistern, all of it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. Its first opinion says that even a little יין נסך falling into a big cistern of wine makes the whole cistern forbidden, so one may not even get benefit from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a small forbidden amount can be cancelled in a large permitted amount. This opinion holds that יין נסך is not cancelled, so the entire mixture takes on the strict status of עבודה זרה wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine that was actually poured as an offering to an idol
A cistern or pit, here a big container full of wine
Forbidden to get any benefit from it, not just forbidden to drink
Our משנה

phrases.english: MISHNA: Libation wine
that fell into a cistern
phrases.notes: The cistern is full of permitted wine, so the forbidden wine is now mixed into it.

phrases.english: all of it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about a new case of mixtures, after the earlier discussion of the list of items that forbid a mixture.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יין נסך that falls into a cistern of wine forbids the entire cistern for benefit.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: sell it all, minus the forbidden part's value
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the whole cistern may be sold to a גוי, but the seller may not keep the money that matches the יין נסך inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: All of it may be sold to a גוי, except for the value of the יין נסך in it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה disagrees. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows selling the whole mixture to a גוי and keeping the money, except for the part of the money that pays for the forbidden wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees the wine may not be drunk by a Jew, but he does not let the small forbidden part ruin the value of the whole cistern. The seller only gives up the money for the forbidden portion, so he gets no benefit from the יין נסך itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It may be sold to a non-Jew
The value or money paid for something

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
all of it may be sold to a non-Jew,
except for the value of the libation wine in it.
phrases.notes: He means the seller may keep the money, except for the portion that pays for the forbidden wine.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two views: the תנא קמא forbids the whole cistern for benefit, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets it be sold to a גוי, minus the value of the forbidden wine.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: יִמָּכֵר כּוּלּוֹ לְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing, more lenient opinion on the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole mixture may be sold to a גוי, except for the money matching the value of the יין נסך.

steps.title: רב: follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only for a barrel among barrels
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only when a closed barrel of יין נסך got lost among permitted barrels, not when the wine itself mixed into other wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל when a barrel is mixed among barrels, but not when wine is mixed into wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב decides the הלכה like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but only in a limited case: a whole barrel mixed up among other barrels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב splits the case in two. If the forbidden barrel is just lost among other barrels, the lenient view applies. If the forbidden wine actually poured into the other wine, which is the משנה's own case, רב does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows this opinion
A whole barrel mixed up among other barrels, with no liquid mixed together
The wine itself poured into and blended with other wine

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה's case is wine falling into a cistern, which is wine in wine. So רב is actually saying the הלכה does NOT follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה's own case, only in the barrel case.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
when a barrel is mixed among barrels,
but not when wine is mixed into wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל חָבִית בְּחָבִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the מחלוקת in the משנה and limits the lenient view to one kind of mixture.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only for a barrel mixed among barrels, not for wine mixed into wine.

steps.title: שמואל: follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even for wine in wine
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even when the wine itself mixed into other wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Even wine mixed in wine.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל argues with רב. He says the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in every case, even when the forbidden wine poured into the permitted wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, there is no difference between a lost barrel and blended liquid. In both cases the whole mixture can be sold to a גוי, minus the value of the יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Even wine mixed in wine.
phrases.notes: He means: even there the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב by extending the ruling to wine mixed in wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even when wine mixed into wine.

steps.title: Three more chains of אמוראים agree with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists three more teachers, רבי יוחנן, רבי חנינא, and רבה בר אבוה, who all say the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even for wine in wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said: Even wine in wine. And likewise רבי שמואל בר נחמני said that רבי חנינא said: Even wine in wine. And likewise רב נחמן said that רבה בר אבוה said: Even wine in wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds three more opinions, each passed down by a student, all agreeing with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here; the step adds weight. Many important teachers stand on שמואל's side, so רב's limit looks like a minority view.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise said, showing agreement with the opinion just quoted

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: And likewise Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even wine in wine.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: And likewise Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Chanina said:
Even wine in wine.
And likewise Rav Nachman said
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Even wine in wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's view with three more chains of teachers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן, רבי חנינא, and רבה בר אבוה all rule like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even for wine in wine.

steps.title: רב נחמן's practical ruling: three cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives the practical הלכה: real יין נסך mixed as liquid is forbidden, a barrel among barrels is permitted, and סתם יינם is permitted even when mixed as liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The practical הלכה is: actual יין נסך, wine in wine, is forbidden; a barrel among barrels is permitted; סתם יינם, even wine in wine, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן sums up how to actually rule. He splits the cases by what kind of forbidden wine it is and how it got mixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For wine that was truly poured to an idol, he is strict like רב: only a lost barrel gets the lenient sale. For סתם יינם, wine only forbidden out of worry it was poured to an idol, he is lenient like שמואל, even when it blended in. 'Permitted' here means it may be sold in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's way.

keyTerms.meaning: The law as it is actually practiced
Ordinary wine of a גוי, forbidden only because it might have been poured to an idol
Permitted, here meaning it may be sold as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught

steps.confusionAlert: מוּתָּר here does not mean a Jew may drink the wine. It means the mixture may be sold to a גוי, minus the value of the forbidden wine, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught.
steps.whatToRemember: Real יין נסך mixed as liquid is forbidden; a barrel lost among barrels may be sold; סתם יינם may be sold even when mixed as liquid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law and shows that the stricter or more lenient approach can depend on how serious the forbidden wine is.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The practical halacha is:
actual libation wine, wine in wine — forbidden;
a barrel among barrels — permitted;
ordinary wine of non-Jews
even wine in wine — permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the רב versus שמואל dispute by splitting the cases between real יין נסך and סתם יינם.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Real יין נסך: wine in wine is forbidden, barrel among barrels may be sold. סתם יינם: even wine in wine may be sold, like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
